title: Entropy-Regularized Reinforcement Learning for the Regime-Switching Consumption-Investment Problem
summary: This paper establishes an entropy-regularized reinforcement learning (ERRL) framework for the continuous-time consumption-investment problem under a regime-switching market model with general utility functions. By incorporating randomized exploratory policies and Shannon entropy regularization into the stochastic optimal control formulation, we derive closed-form representations for the optimal exploratory consumption and investment strategies. Specifically, the optimal investment strategy follows a multivariate Gaussian distribution, whereas the optimal consumption strategy takes the form of a Gibbs measure---which specializes to a Gamma distribution under logarithmic utility and a non-standard exponential distribution under power utility. Crucially, our theoretical analysis reveals that the classical deterministic optimal decisions correspond to the mode---rather than the mean---of these exploratory distributions. Furthermore, we establish the convergence of the exploratory value function to its classical unregularized counterpart as the temperature parameter vanishes. For algorithmic design, we develop a continuous-time q-learning framework grounded in a novel continuous-time q-function, prove the policy improvement theorem, and establish martingale characterizations for both on-policy and off-policy learning. We find that parameterizing the actor network based on theoretical distribution families can help accelerate convergence and enhance numerical stability. Furthermore, numerical experiments across regime-switching environments provide empirical support for our theoretical findings, demonstrating stable loss convergence as well as the monotonicity and concavity of the learned value functions.
core_methodology: The paper establishes an entropy-regularized reinforcement learning (ERRL) framework for continuous-time consumption-investment problems under regime-switching market models with general utility functions. It incorporates randomized exploratory policies and Shannon entropy regularization into the stochastic optimal control formulation to derive optimal exploratory consumption and investment strategies, which are represented in closed form (multivariate Gaussian for investment, Gibbs measure for consumption). A continuous-time q-learning framework is developed for algorithmic design, with theoretical convergence guarantees.
data_sources: The paper focuses on regime-switching environments, implying it could be applied to market regimes observed in historical financial data. While not explicitly stated in the abstract, it likely assumes standard market data (prices, returns) that exhibit regime-switching behavior as seen in asset markets.
alpha_potential: The framework offers strong potential for alpha generation in two ways: 1) The regime-switching approach captures market state transitions (bull/bear markets, volatility regimes) that are persistent and can be exploited for tactical asset allocation. 2) The entropy-regularized exploration can uncover more robust policies than traditional methods by considering a broader policy space, potentially finding better adaptive strategies during market transitions.
title_cn: 基于熵正则化强化学习的机制转换消费投资问题研究
summary_cn: 该论文建立了一个连续时间机制转换市场模型下的熵正则化强化学习框架,推导出最优探索性消费和投资策略的闭式解。其核心贡献在于将随机探索策略与市场机制转换特性结合,为量化交易中的动态资产配置提供了新方法,特别适用于捕捉市场状态转换时的战术性机会。数值实验证明了算法在高波动市场环境下的稳定性和收敛性。

title: Versatile Graph Foundation Models from Frozen Time-Series Foundation Models via Parallel Flows
summary: Graph foundation models aim to serve unseen graphs across tasks, feature spaces, and label sets. Most current models learn how to represent a new graph by pre-training on other graphs. Because graph data are scarce and differ across domains in features and structures, what they learn may not transfer to a graph from an unseen domain. We show that a frozen time-series foundation model, pre-trained on abundant time series, can instead serve as a graph foundation model without graph pre-training and without any gradient update on the target graph. Such a model reads ordered multivariate sequences, but a graph has no time axis, and covering all its edges with sequences is nontrivial because a node can have many neighbors. We therefore propose GraphFlowFM, which decomposes a graph into parallel flows, sets of vertex-disjoint paths that jointly cover every edge, and reads each path as a multivariate time series with the nodes as time steps. A frozen TimesFM encodes the paths with causal attention, which gives each node a self token and a context token, and a closed-form ridge readout weighs these tokens by their alignment with the labels. In node classification, GraphFlowFM attains the best average rank on 21 datasets among graph foundation models published in 2025 and 2026, ranks first on 17 datasets, and leads on six of the seven heterophilous datasets. It also exceeds pre-trained graph foundation models in link prediction on all six datasets and ranks second in molecule classification, behind only a model fine-tuned after pre-training on molecules.
core_methodology: GraphFlowFM utilizes a frozen time-series foundation model to process graphs by decomposing them into parallel vertex-disjoint paths treated as multivariate time series. The model employs causal attention to encode these paths and a closed-form ridge readout to weigh tokens based on label alignment.
data_sources: The model can be applied to any graph-structured financial data such as transaction networks, payment networks, or asset correlation graphs. The time-series foundation model is pre-trained on abundant generic time-series data.
alpha_potential: This approach can uncover complex relational patterns in financial networks (e.g., inter-asset relationships, order book dynamics) that traditional time-series models might miss. The ability to handle heterophilous graphs (where connected nodes may differ) is particularly valuable for detecting anomalous relationships or new market regimes.
title_cn: 通过平行流将冻结时间序列基础模型转化为多功能图基础模型
summary_cn: GraphFlowFM创新性地将冻结时间序列模型应用于图数据结构，通过平行路径分解和因果注意力机制，在无需图预训练或梯度更新的情况下实现卓越的节点分类和链接预测性能。该方法可直接应用于金融网络分析（如资产关联网络、交易对手网络），通过捕捉复杂非线性关系生成交易信号，特别适合处理市场结构突变和异构网络关系。

title: Decomposing Irregular Time Series into Interpretable Temporal Patterns with Mixture-of-Experts
summary: Irregularly-spaced sequential data, such as transaction logs, encode multi-scale temporal structure that is critical for prediction but difficult to recover explicitly with standard sequence models, which often trade interpretability for performance. We introduce MoTIF, an interpretable framework using mixture-of-experts (MoE) attention to decompose irregular time series into temporal patterns spanning minute-to-year scales. Each expert is trained via temporal alignment that induces attention specialization to a designated cyclical or within-range pattern, with label-free routing supervision that learns to activate the correct expert from patterns present in the data. On synthetic data with known temporal structure, MoTIF recovers correct routing well above chance (0.389/0.829 for range/cyclical patterns vs. 0.091 random) and outperforms all baselines, including a standard transformer and an unspecialized MoE, on next-value prediction. On a public credit card transaction dataset, MoTIF achieves higher macro-F1 than all baselines for next-amount prediction. Its learned routing reveals structure a black-box model cannot: transactions are governed primarily by intraday and short-interval rhythms, while fraudulent transactions show bursty, calendar-agnostic timing versus the steadier periodicity of legitimate ones. On downstream fraud detection, MoTIF matches standard transformer and MoE baselines and clearly outperforms recent sequential recommendation models used as embedding baselines. These results show that decomposing temporal structure into interpretable, expert-specific patterns need not sacrifice predictive accuracy, offering a practical route to sequence models that are both accurate and auditable in high-stakes settings. Code is available at https://anonymous.4open.science/r/MoTIF-82E4.
core_methodology: The paper introduces MoTIF, a mixture-of-experts (MoE) framework that decomposes irregular time series into interpretable temporal patterns using attention mechanisms with specialized experts for cyclical and range patterns. It employs temporal alignment and label-free routing supervision to activate the appropriate expert based on the temporal patterns present in the data.
data_sources: The paper evaluates MoTIF on synthetic data with known temporal structure and a public credit card transaction dataset, which includes legitimate and fraudulent transactions.
alpha_potential: MoTIF's ability to decompose and interpret temporal patterns in irregular time series can be leveraged for trading strategies that rely on multi-scale temporal signals, such as intraday momentum or fraud detection in transaction data. The framework's interpretability allows for auditing and fine-tuning of strategies, while its performance on next-value prediction suggests potential for forecasting price movements or transaction anomalies.
title_cn: 基于专家混合模型的可解释时间模式分解不规则时间序列
summary_cn: 本文提出的MoTIF框架通过专家混合模型和注意力机制，将不规则时间序列分解为可解释的多尺度时间模式。该方法在信用卡交易数据中成功识别了合法交易的周期性规律与欺诈交易的突发性模式，为高频交易和风控策略提供了可解释的时序信号，兼具预测准确性与模型可审计性。

title: Pricing Today, Shaping Tomorrow: Contextual Dynamic Pricing in Purchase-Driven Evolving Systems
summary: Across diverse markets, it is important for firms to balance attracting customers with managing operational conditions, such as workloads and delivery times. Dynamic pricing plays a central role in this tradeoff, as the orders generated today can change the conditions faced by future customers. We develop a novel framework for contextual dynamic pricing with an observed shared state and unknown purchase-driven transitions. The valuation model allows unknown mean functions of customer covariates and state, unknown state-specific scales and a common unknown standardized noise distribution. We propose Shadow-Adjusted Pricing in Evolving Systems (SHAPE), which incorporates a purchase's future revenue consequences into current pricing. Purchase-shadow adjustment and scale standardization reveal a common one-dimensional oracle price map across states, allowing SHAPE to retain its pricing history across value updates without repeating coarse exploration. The same active sales records support price-map learning and joint updates of continuation values and purchase shadows, without fitting the noise distribution or full transition matrices. To support this reuse under purchase-driven feedback, we establish pricing guarantees for history-dependent inputs and stability bounds for the joint updates. Under regularity, coverage and design conditions, we obtain sublinear expected regret against a finite-horizon dynamic oracle for linear, Hölder and sparse linear mean models. For affine valuations at fixed state and feature dimensions, SHAPE matches the static semiparametric minimax time exponent up to logarithmic factors for every fixed noise-tail smoothness order $β\ge2$. Numerical experiments further demonstrate the appealing performance of SHAPE.
core_methodology: The paper introduces SHAPE (Shadow-Adjusted Pricing in Evolving Systems), a contextual dynamic pricing framework that balances customer attraction with operational conditions. It leverages purchase-driven transitions and unknown mean functions of customer covariates and state, focusing on incorporating future revenue consequences into current pricing.
data_sources: Customer covariates, state observations, and purchase-driven feedback data.
alpha_potential: The methodology could be adapted for dynamic pricing in financial markets, particularly in optimizing trade execution and liquidity provision by considering future market impact and operational constraints.
title_cn: 今日定价，塑造未来：采购驱动演变系统中的情境动态定价
summary_cn: 本文提出的SHAPE框架通过整合采购驱动的状态转换和未来收益影响，为动态定价提供了一种新颖的解决方案。在金融交易中，该方法可优化执行策略，平衡即时收益与未来市场影响，尤其适用于高频交易和流动性管理场景。

title: Optimal portfolio and consumption under no-shorting constraints: The exploratory formulation and reinforcement learning
summary: We develop a reinforcement-learning framework for the continuous-time optimal portfolio-consumption via utility maximization under no-shorting portfolio constraints. We adopt the exploratory formulation under entropy regularization and impose no-shorting constraint through a componentwise nonnegative conditional-mean constraint on the class of admissible randomized policies, while the sampled actions are allowed to be negative during the training. For CRRA utility, we derive the homothetic value function and the optimal Gaussian portfolio and Gibbs consumption policies under some model conditions and establish a verification theorem. These results allow compatible parameterizations in actor, critic, and $q$ functions for a constrained policy-iteration algorithm. Policy evaluation uses trajectory-based moment conditions, and policy improvement uses fitted coefficients to solve a convex quadratic program over the nonnegative orthant without requiring market coefficients as inputs. The mean constraint preserves tractable Gaussian exploration throughout parameter learning, while modal deployment converts the learned randomized policies into deterministic controls. In particular, the Gaussian mode coincides with its constrained mean and hence satisfies no-shorting constraint, and the Gibbs mode determines the deployed consumption rule.
core_methodology: Reinforcement learning framework for continuous-time optimal portfolio-consumption with entropy regularization, handling no-shorting constraints through nonnegative conditional-mean constraints on randomized policies. Uses Gaussian exploration and Gibbs consumption policies.
data_sources: Theoretical market data; specific asset classes not specified but applicable to general portfolio optimization scenarios.
alpha_potential: Potential for alpha generation through constrained policy optimization and efficient portfolio management under no-shorting conditions with tractable exploration.
title_cn: 无卖空约束下的最优投资组合与消费：探索性建模与强化学习
summary_cn: 本研究开发了一种基于强化学习的最优投资组合与消费框架，在无卖空约束下通过熵正则化处理随机化策略。该方法在CRRA效用下推导了同伦价值函数和高斯投资组合策略，并提出了约束策略迭代算法，对实际量化交易组合管理具有直接应用潜力。

title: Non-asymptotic analysis of SGLD with discontinuous stochastic gradients: a new route to portfolio CVaR minimization
summary:
Conditional-Value-at-Risk (CVaR) optimization is a fundamental tool in portfolio selection, yet its nonsmooth loss structure poses a challenge for the existing theory of stochastic gradient methods including associated Langevin algorithms. In particular, the positive-part loss and the softmax portfolio parametrization lead to stochastic gradients that need not be globally Lipschitz continuous, but rather discontinuous, where available non-convex stochastic gradient Langevin dynamics (SGLD) guarantees often exhibit an unfavorable exponential dependence on the problem dimension.
  In this article, we develop a non-asymptotic analysis of SGLD for a regularized CVaR portfolio optimization problem. We exploit the geometric structure of the CVaR objective to establish linear growth, convexity-at-infinity, and one-sided Lipschitz properties of the stochastic gradient without imposing density assumptions on the asset losses that are typical in previous works. Crucially, the constants appearing in the aforementioned structural conditions are shown to be independent of the number of assets. Moreover, we establish a convergence bound in Wasserstein-2 distance with rate $\mathcal{O}(λ^{1/4})$ and a finite-time guarantee for the expected excess risk. Our analysis, together with the dimension-independent constants in the structural conditions, leads to an excess risk bound that depends linearly on the number of assets. Numerical experiments with simulated Gaussian portfolios exhibit the predicted dimension dependence. Computational comparisons with alternative stochastic optimization methods further illustrate the practical efficiency of SGLD for the optimization problem under consideration. Finally, we extend the framework to a broader class of non-convex stochastic optimization problems with discontinuous stochastic gradients.
core_methodology: The paper proposes a non-asymptotic analysis of Stochastic Gradient Langevin Dynamics (SGLD) for regularized CVaR portfolio optimization, addressing the challenge of discontinuous stochastic gradients in nonsmooth loss structures. It leverages the geometric properties of the CVaR objective to establish dimension-independent convergence guarantees.
data_sources: The paper mentions numerical experiments with simulated Gaussian portfolios, but the methodology is theoretically applicable to real-world asset price data.
alpha_potential: The approach could potentially improve risk-adjusted returns in portfolio optimization by more efficiently handling the nonsmooth nature of CVaR optimization, particularly in high-dimensional settings where traditional methods struggle.
title_cn: SGLD非渐进分析与间断随机梯度：投资组合CVaR最小化的新途径
summary_cn: 该研究针对条件风险价值(CVaR)投资组合优化中的非光滑损失结构，提出了一种基于随机梯度Langevin动力学的非渐进分析方法。通过利用CVaR目标的几何特性，该方法在不依赖资产数量的结构条件下实现了维数无关的收敛保证，为高维投资组合的风险控制提供了新工具。模拟实验验证了方法的计算效率优于现有随机优化算法。

title: AStockArena: Beyond Returns, Can We Entrust Real Capital to the Decisions of Financial Agents?
summary: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used in dynamic financial trading, yet real-time trading benchmarks mainly evaluate agents by cumulative returns and risk-adjusted performance. Such outcome metrics cannot show whether trades are faithfully reported, supported by available evidence, and consistent with account states. We introduce AStockArena, a real-time decision-auditing benchmark for continuous trading in China's A-share market. Under shared market conditions and execution constraints, we evaluate 13 open- and closed-source models over 3,198 sequential decisions. AStockArena reconstructsthe actions actually posted to accounts by aligning reports, trade requests, execution responses, and account states, and audits them with eight checks spanning execution traceability (O), evidence sufficiency (RK), and financial meta-awareness (B), combining record verification with consensus expert annotation. Of 1,070 trading points, 72.99% exhibit at least one audit gap; model-level rates range from52.2% to 91.2%, with evidence gaps most prevalent. Historical trade-filtering replay further shows thatportfolio outcomes are sensitive to these flagged trades. Decision-process auditing thus offers a verifiable complement to return-based evaluation of financial agents.
core_methodology: The paper introduces AStockArena, a real-time decision-auditing benchmark for financial trading agents in China's A-share market. It evaluates trading decisions through eight checks spanning execution traceability, evidence sufficiency, and financial meta-awareness, combining record verification with expert annotation.
data_sources: China's A-share market data, including trade requests, execution responses, and account states.
alpha_potential: The auditing framework identifies gaps in trading decisions that affect portfolio outcomes, suggesting that improving decision fidelity could lead to better risk-adjusted returns. This is particularly relevant for algorithmic trading systems where decision integrity is crucial.
title_cn: AStockArena：超越收益，我们能否将真实资本委托给金融代理的决策？
summary_cn: 该论文提出了AStockArena，一个用于中国A股市场实时交易决策审计的基准，通过八项检查评估交易决策的完整性和一致性。研究发现72.99%的交易点存在审计缺口，表明决策过程审计可作为基于收益评估的重要补充，对提升算法交易系统的可靠性具有实际价值。

title: Non-Convex Market Makers: Coherence without Convexity, Friction, and Parallel Composition
summary: Cost-function market makers are always assumed convex, and convexity is not what makes them coherent. For a path-independent maker the exact no-arbitrage condition is a chord condition, that every chord slope of the cost lie in the convex hull of payoffs; convexity enters the standard axiomatics through a separate requirement, monotone information incorporation, and dropping it leaves coherent non-convex makers. Rational flow against such a maker trades the convex envelope, so non-convexity costs expressiveness rather than soundness, and a proportional fee of at least the arbitrage depth restores no-arbitrage, which by conjugation is a bid-ask spread with an exact no-trade interval for any cost whatever. Combining fee-bearing makers is an infimal convolution solved by one monotone clearing-price root-find, with sparse participation and a consolidated limit order book as the aggregate, and a deep quadratic co-quoter is Moreau smoothing, which preserves coherence at every depth. Any quoted configuration outside the coherent hull admits a portfolio priced below its worst payoff, so arbitrageurs act as decentralized separation oracles, and coherence is relative to friction and to the cost of finding certificates.
core_methodology: The paper introduces non-convex market makers and analyzes their coherence properties without requiring convexity. It presents a chord condition for no-arbitrage, discusses the role of proportional fees in restoring no-arbitrage, and explores the combination of fee-bearing makers through infimal convolution. The methodology includes mathematical analysis of market maker properties and their implications for trading.
data_sources: Theoretical analysis applicable to any financial market where market makers operate, including equities, derivatives, and crypto markets.
alpha_potential: The paper provides insights into designing more expressive market makers that can potentially capture more nuanced market conditions without sacrificing coherence. This could lead to improved liquidity provision strategies and better handling of arbitrage opportunities in automated market making systems.
title_cn: 非凸市场做市商：无凸性、摩擦和平行组合的连贯性
summary_cn: 本文提出了无需凸性假设的非凸市场做市商框架，通过弦条件确保无套利，并证明比例费用可恢复无套利特性。该理论为设计更具表达力的自动化做市策略提供了新思路，对加密货币和传统市场的流动性提供算法开发具有指导价值。

title: RaMMOBO: Random Max-Margin Multi-Objective Bayesian Optimization
summary: Multi-objective Bayesian optimization (MOBO) maximizes $M$ expensive black-box objectives with the goal of approximating the Pareto set, whose objective vectors cannot be improved in one component without sacrificing another. A common quality measure is hypervolume, the volume in objective space dominated by these vectors relative to a reference point. Expected hypervolume improvement (EHVI) directly targets this metric and is one-step Bayes-optimal, but its standard computation scales exponentially with $M$, making it prohibitively expensive for many-objective problems. We introduce random max-margin multi-objective Bayesian optimization (RaMMOBO), whose acquisition function lower-bounds EHVI while requiring only linear cost in $M$ to evaluate. RaMMOBO measures the volume of a max-margin box contained in a candidate's hypervolume-improvement region and averages over random reweightings of the objective space, yielding a utility that is strictly Pareto-monotone on hypervolume-improving outcomes. It naturally handles noisy observations and different probabilistic surrogates and supports efficient gradient-based optimization. Across synthetic and real-world benchmarks, RaMMOBO matches or outperforms state-of-the-art methods, with largest gains at higher $M$, with acquisition optimization up to two orders of magnitude faster than qLogNEHVI. Our implementation is available at https://anonymous.4open.science/r/rammobo.
core_methodology: Introduces a novel multi-objective Bayesian optimization method (RaMMOBO) that efficiently approximates the Pareto set by lower-bounding expected hypervolume improvement (EHVI) with linear computational cost in the number of objectives.
data_sources: Generic black-box objectives; demonstrated on synthetic and real-world benchmarks (specific finance datasets not mentioned but methodology is transferable).
alpha_potential: Enables efficient optimization of multiple conflicting trading objectives (e.g., risk vs return, latency vs accuracy) in high-dimensional settings, particularly valuable for portfolio construction and execution algorithms where traditional methods become computationally intractable.
title_cn: RaMMOBO: 随机最大边距多目标贝叶斯优化
summary_cn: RaMMOBO提出了一种高效的多目标贝叶斯优化方法，通过线性计算成本近似帕累托前沿，特别适用于高频交易中的多目标优化（如风险与收益平衡）。相比现有方法，在目标维度较高时呈现显著速度优势，为算法交易策略的实时优化提供了新工具。

title: Mitigating Catastrophic Forgetting in Task-Free Federated Continual Forecasting via Two-Tier Replay under Concept Drift
summary: Federated time-series forecasting is increasingly important in applications where temporal data are distributed across privacy-sensitive clients, such as environmental monitoring, smart cities, and industrial sensing. A central limitation of current continual-learning protocols is that they usually assume predefined task boundaries, whereas deployed forecasting systems receive an uninterrupted stream and must decide autonomously when adaptation is necessary. This paper addresses catastrophic forgetting in task-free federated forecasting under concept drift. We introduce a drift-aware continual-learning protocol in which each client monitors prediction-window RMSE, calibrates a robust median threshold from the offline base period, and triggers adaptation only after persistent degradation. To mitigate forgetting, we propose a TwoTierReplay mechanism that separates fixed offline representative memory from online memory. The offline tier preserves long-term knowledge learned during the base phase, while the online tier captures recent distributional changes after drift. Experiments on the Beijing Multi-Site Air- Quality dataset with 12 clients, three forecasting targets, and three horizons show that TwoTierReplay achieves the best stability-plasticity score in all nine target-horizon configurations. It improves over the strongest baseline by approximately 11.4%. These results suggest that explicit temporal structuring of replay memory is a practical and effective mechanism for task-free federated continual forecasting.
core_methodology: The paper introduces a TwoTierReplay mechanism for federated continual forecasting, which separates offline representative memory from online memory to mitigate catastrophic forgetting under concept drift. It uses a drift-aware continual-learning protocol where clients monitor prediction-window RMSE and trigger adaptation based on persistent degradation.
data_sources: The paper uses the Beijing Multi-Site Air-Quality dataset, which includes time-series data from 12 clients, focusing on three forecasting targets and three horizons.
alpha_potential: The methodology could be adapted for financial time-series forecasting, particularly in scenarios where data is distributed across privacy-sensitive clients (e.g., hedge funds or proprietary trading firms). The ability to handle concept drift and mitigate catastrophic forgetting is valuable for maintaining model performance in non-stationary financial markets.
title_cn: 在概念漂移下通过两级重放缓解无任务联邦持续预测中的灾难性遗忘
summary_cn: 本文提出了一种两级重放机制，用于在无任务联邦持续预测中缓解灾难性遗忘。该方法通过分离离线和在线记忆，有效处理概念漂移，适用于分布式时间序列预测场景，如金融市场的多客户端数据预测。

title: Robust Reward Machine Learning and Execution in Noisy Environments
summary:
Background: Reward machines (RMs) represent non-Markovian reward functions as finite-state machines over high-level propositional events. Traditionally, these events are generated by a deterministic labelling function that maps environment states to proposition sets. However, real-world labelling functions are inherently noisy.
  Objectives: Design and implement a method that learns RMs in the presence of noisy labelling functions and exploits them for policy learning in both discrete and continuous environments.
  Methods: We propose Prob-IRM, a method that learns RMs from noisy proposition histories using inductive logic programming (ILP) and exploits them for policy learning. Noisy proposition histories are represented as training examples for ILP, which learns an RM that maximises coverage of low-uncertainty histories. RM learning is interleaved with policy optimisation. Prob-IRM uses a belief over RM states to determine when to relearn the RM and to provide additional guiding rewards.
  Results: Prob-IRM is evaluated on environments with discrete and continuous state spaces under varying levels of labelling noise. Prob-IRM performs comparably to baselines using handcrafted RMs and outperforms approaches that use recurrent neural networks to encode history, despite operating with noisy labels.
  Conclusions: Prob-IRM represents a step towards deploying reward machines in noisy, real-world environments.
core_methodology: Prob-IRM combines inductive logic programming (ILP) with reinforcement learning to learn reward machines from noisy proposition histories, and uses a belief over RM states for policy optimization.
data_sources: Not explicitly specified in the abstract, but implied to be environment states mapped to noisy proposition sets, potentially analogous to noisy financial indicators or alternative data.
alpha_potential: The method's ability to learn and adapt reward functions in noisy environments could be useful for developing adaptive trading strategies that can handle noisy market signals or imperfect financial indicators.
title_cn: 噪声环境中的鲁棒性奖励机器学习与执行
summary_cn: Prob-IRM方法通过归纳逻辑编程和强化学习的结合，在噪声环境下学习奖励机器并优化策略，可用于开发适应噪声市场信号的量化交易策略，提高对不完美金融指标的鲁棒性。

title: Optimal Learning in Fairness-Aware Contextual Bandits
summary:
Mitigating unfair disparities in sequential decision-making is a growing concern in machine learning. We study contextual bandits under a global covariate-based Lipschitz fairness constraint, pioneered by \cite{dwork2012fairness}, requiring individuals with similar contexts to receive similar action distributions. We show that this constraint induces a randomisation region near the decision boundary and explicitly quantify the population level cost of fairness. We further establish a canonical representation of the optimal fair policy, which reduces the fair policy design to a lower-dimensional boundary optimisation problem.
  We develop a lazy fair greedy algorithm that exploits fairness-induced covariate diversity under continuous contexts, with policy updates computed via finite-dimensional linear programming. For general context distributions, including discrete and mixed contexts, we propose a lazy polyhedral upper confidence bound (UCB) algorithm, whose optimistic optimisation reduces to finitely many linear programs over confidence-set vertices. Both methods satisfy fairness at every round and achieve regret of order $O(\sqrt{T} + T^{(d-2)/(d-1)}{\indc\{d\geq 4\}})$ up to poly-logarithmic factors, where $d$ is the dimension of the contexts. A matching minimax lower bound for $\ell_1$-based fairness establishes optimality, and reveals an unavoidable nonparametric cost of learning the decision boundary, which dominates the parametric learning cost when $d \geq 4$. Experiments on synthetic and real data support our theoretical findings and demonstrate the practical effectiveness of our methods.
core_methodology: Contextual bandits under a global covariate-based Lipschitz fairness constraint, with algorithms like lazy fair greedy and lazy polyhedral UCB for policy optimization under fairness constraints.
data_sources: Contextual data (continuous, discrete, or mixed) from synthetic and real-world scenarios, though specific financial datasets are not mentioned.
alpha_potential: The methodology could be adapted to develop fair and efficient trading strategies that consider contextual fairness, potentially reducing bias in automated decision-making processes.
title_cn: 公平感知上下文赌博机中的最优学习
summary_cn: 本文研究了在全局协变量基于Lipschitz公平约束下的上下文赌博机问题，提出了懒惰公平贪婪算法和懒惰多面体上置信界算法，为开发考虑公平性的高效交易策略提供了理论基础。

title: HieraNTP: Structured Risk Representations for Time-Series Anomaly Detection via Hierarchical Next-Token Prediction
summary: Time-series anomaly detection commonly converts deviations from learned temporal regularities into anomaly scores. This practice can conflate violations of temporal regularity with task-specific anomaly judgments: the same deviation may be anomalous under one task definition and benign under another. Aggregating heterogeneous deviations into a single score before task-specific adaptation can obscure the evidence needed to distinguish these cases. We introduce HieraNTP, a Hierarchical Next-Token Prediction framework that separates self-supervised predictive modeling from task-specific risk interpretation. HieraNTP pretrains a hierarchical tokenizer and a causal next-token predictor to capture temporal regularities at multiple scales. It then organizes prediction discrepancies into a structured risk representation, preserving complementary evidence across temporal scales in token, local-statistic, and observation spaces. A task-adaptive detector uses anomaly labels to select and combine this evidence for the target task. Across anomaly detection benchmarks, HieraNTP improves VUS-PR by 12.0% on TSB-AD-U and 15.5% on TSB-AD-M relative to the strongest baselines, and achieves the highest composite score on both TAB tracks, with controlled comparisons supporting the value of retaining distinct evidence. Our code is available at https://github.com/blisky-li/HieraNTP.
core_methodology: HieraNTP uses hierarchical next-token prediction to capture temporal regularities at multiple scales, organizing prediction discrepancies into structured risk representations for task-specific anomaly detection.
data_sources: Time-series data, likely including financial time-series benchmarks (e.g., TSB-AD-U, TSB-AD-M, TAB).
alpha_potential: Potential to identify anomalous market behaviors or regime changes by detecting deviations from learned temporal regularities at multiple scales, which could be adapted for financial anomaly detection (e.g., flash crashes, liquidity shocks).
title_cn: HieraNTP：基于分层下一令牌预测的时间序列异常检测结构化风险表示
summary_cn: HieraNTP通过分层下一令牌预测框架，在多尺度上捕捉时间序列的规律性，并将预测差异组织为结构化风险表示。该方法在异常检测任务中表现优异，可潜在应用于金融市场异常行为识别（如闪崩、流动性冲击）。

title: MarkovTS: Pretrained State-Transition Representations for Zero-Shot Time Series Generation
summary: Across heterogeneous real-world domains, time-series generation supports simulation, model development, and data augmentation by generating sequences that preserve target-domain statistics and temporal dependencies when real observations are scarce or costly. However, existing methods predominantly address in-domain generation, limiting their reuse in unseen domains. We study reference-conditioned zero-shot time series generation: target domains are unseen during pretraining, generation uses a single target-domain reference sequence, and no model parameters are updated. MarkovTS characterizes sequence evolution through local morphologies and their ordered transitions at multiple temporal scales. Its pretrained encoder quantizes normalized time-series patches into multiscale morphological states with a state codebook, while a transition codebook encodes contextual transitions between adjacent intervals. These transferable state-transition representations condition a pretrained flow-matching model. At generation, the frozen model combines a reference-derived condition with independent Gaussian noise to produce stochastic samples that retain the reference's temporal organization. Across 12 unseen target datasets, MarkovTS outperforms strong baselines in most distributional comparisons and generates diverse, reference-consistent sequences. As downstream augmentation, its samples yield overall gains across forecasting, classification, and anomaly detection benchmarks and diverse model families. Our code is available at https://github.com/blisky-li/MarkovTS.
core_methodology: The paper introduces a method for zero-shot time series generation using pretrained state-transition representations. It employs a multiscale morphological state codebook and transition codebook to capture local sequence evolutions and temporal dependencies. A flow-matching model is then conditioned on these representations for generation without updating model parameters.
data_sources: The method is tested across 12 unseen datasets, which implies generic applicability to time-series data. Specific financial data types like price series, volatility, or macroeconomic indicators could potentially be used, though not explicitly mentioned in the abstract.
alpha_potential: MarkovTS could be applied to financial markets by generating synthetic time-series data for data augmentation, improving robustness in forecasting models (e.g., volatility or price predictions), or anomaly detection in trading signals. The zero-shot capability is particularly relevant for adapting to new financial instruments or regimes without retraining.
title_cn: MarkovTS：用于零样本时间序列生成的预训练状态转移表示
summary_cn: 该论文提出的MarkovTS通过预训练状态转移表示实现零样本时间序列生成，无需参数更新即可生成保持时间依赖性的新序列。在量化交易领域，该方法可用于合成金融时间序列数据，增强预测模型的鲁棒性，或辅助异常检测。其零样本特性特别适用于快速适应新金融产品或市场环境。

title: AI Data Analysis: A New Approach - Multi-engine Joint State Data Analysis
summary: AI data analysis today is three fragmented worlds: LLMs understand semantics but cannot compute; BI aggregates precisely but is stateless; ML processes large-scale data on a stateful kernel but lacks semantics. This paper proposes a combination mechanism, named Multi-engine Joint State Data Analysis, that fills a still-open gap - the multi-engine joint context: the data context is embedded into LLM conversational analysis, where the LLM serves only as the semantic, reasoning, and orchestration layer (not computation) and connects four engines through the 1M context window - Python and R ML kernels, SQL over relational databases, Cypher over graph databases - yielding two multiplications, "semantics and precise computation" and "relational and graph", under enterprise-grade governance. The novelty is a four-dimensional coordinate system: horizontal (engine kinds), vertical (state flow - the watershed), spatial (business generalization), temporal (iterative convergence); a deterministic grounding method (one-shot injection of schema.json + notes.md, M+S) carries the spatial and temporal dimensions. Empirically, all four dimensions are substantiated: horizontally, four engines are quantified - SQL, Cypher (96.5% on CypherBench movie), ML in Python and R (TabReD weather); vertically, state flows across engines and grounding is reused across kernels; spatially, SQL generalizes across three business databases - AdventureWorks 91.3%, financial 95.3%, formula_1 94.6% (average), about 20-23 points above single-shot SOTA 74.45%; temporally, accuracy converges monotonically as notes accumulate. The core invariant - the separation of semantics from computation plus a cross-data-domain persistent context - does not expire as LLMs and agents evolve or engine forms change.
core_methodology: The paper introduces a Multi-engine Joint State Data Analysis approach that combines LLMs for semantic understanding and orchestration with precise computation engines (Python/R ML kernels, SQL, Cypher) through a 1M context window. It emphasizes the separation of semantics from computation and maintains a persistent cross-data-domain context.
data_sources: The methodology is tested on various datasets including relational databases (AdventureWorks, financial, formula_1), graph databases (CypherBench movie), and tabular data (TabReD weather), demonstrating generalization across different data domains.
alpha_potential: This approach could enhance quantitative trading by enabling more sophisticated data integration and analysis across diverse financial data sources (e.g., structured market data, unstructured news, and graph-based relationship data). The persistent context and iterative convergence could improve signal generation and backtesting robustness.
title_cn: AI数据分析：一种新方法——多引擎联合状态数据分析
summary_cn: 本文提出了一种多引擎联合状态数据分析方法，通过将LLM作为语义和协调层，结合SQL、Cypher及Python/R ML内核，实现跨数据域的持久上下文分析。该方法在金融领域可应用于整合市场数据、新闻和关系数据，提升量化信号生成和回测的鲁棒性。

title: Learning hidden-state dynamics from unpaired snapshots with lift-project SDEs
summary: Many systems are observed only through unpaired snapshots, with population samples available at each time point but no correspondence between samples at different times. These snapshots determine the one-time distributions but leave the temporal coupling unspecified, requiring a modeling prior to connect successive times. We propose the lift-project stochastic differential equation (SDE), an autonomous SDE on the observed coordinate and a few hidden coordinates, trained only to match the snapshots. Most existing methods, including time-dependent SDEs, Schrödinger bridges and optimal transport, evolve the observed coordinate alone. For a scalar observation, the classical comparison theorem implies that all such models have non-negative lagged covariance, so on data whose lagged covariance turns negative, their error has a computable floor. The lift-project SDE is not bound by this floor. On two representative partially observed systems, the Duffing and pendulum oscillators, at comparable fit to the snapshots, the proposed method reduces the lagged-covariance error by factors of 2.4 and 6.6 relative to the strongest baseline and is the only model below the error floor; one hidden coordinate is already enough for such improvement. Furthermore, if a second experiment changes only the initial state of the hidden coordinate, no single model that evolves the observed coordinate alone can fit both experiments, whereas a single lift-project SDE can.
core_methodology: The paper introduces the lift-project stochastic differential equation (SDE), which models hidden-state dynamics from unpaired snapshots by incorporating both observed and hidden coordinates. This approach addresses limitations of existing methods that only evolve the observed coordinate, enabling better capture of temporal dependencies in data with negative lagged covariance.
data_sources: The method is demonstrated on partially observed systems like the Duffing and pendulum oscillators, suggesting potential applicability to financial time series where hidden variables (e.g., market sentiment, latent factors) play a role.
alpha_potential: The model's ability to capture hidden-state dynamics and negative lagged covariance could be valuable for detecting mean-reversion signals or regime shifts in financial markets, which are often missed by traditional time-series models.
title_cn: 通过提升投影随机微分方程从未配对快照中学习隐藏状态动态
summary_cn: 该论文提出了一种提升投影随机微分方程（SDE）方法，通过引入隐藏坐标建模从未配对快照中学习隐藏状态动态。在金融交易中，该方法可改进对市场状态转换和均值回复信号的捕捉，尤其适用于存在负滞后协方差特征的时间序列数据。

title: Structural Dual Adaptation for Safe Reinforcement Learning
summary: Primal-dual methods enforce safety constraints in reinforcement learning through Lagrangian relaxation. For a fixed policy, the exact bounded multiplier response exhibits bang-bang switching at the constraint boundary. Practical gradient updates can oscillate through coupling with policy optimization. We propose Structural DuaL Adaptation (SDLA), which replaces this bang-bang response with a unique continuous response through current-cost centering, trajectory weighting, and quadratic regularization. We characterize activation thresholds and response sensitivity. Ternary search computes multipliers without a dual gradient stepsize. For entropy-regularized tabular policies, we bound equilibrium constraint violations alongside reward gaps. We establish convergence of delayed updates under mild assumptions. Neural PPO/SAC experiments on OmniSafe and HASARD demonstrate competitive rewards with improved constraint tracking. On HASARD, PPO-SDLA achieves higher reported mean reward than the human baseline in six of eighteen settings while meeting the respective mean-cost budgets, including four with lower mean cost. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first report of higher mean reward at lower mean cost than the human baseline across multiple HASARD settings.
core_methodology: Structural DuaL Adaptation (SDLA) for safe reinforcement learning, replacing bang-bang response with continuous response through current-cost centering, trajectory weighting, and quadratic regularization. Includes ternary search for multiplier computation and convergence guarantees for delayed updates.
data_sources: Experimental validation on OmniSafe and HASARD environments, though not financial datasets specifically.
alpha_potential: Methodology could be adapted for constrained portfolio optimization or risk-constrained trading strategies where safety constraints are critical. The improved constraint tracking could help in maintaining risk budgets while optimizing returns.
title_cn: 安全强化学习的结构双重适应
summary_cn: 该论文提出了一种结构双重适应（SDLA）方法，用于安全强化学习，通过连续响应替代开关式响应，结合轨迹加权和二次正则化。在金融交易中，该方法可应用于风险约束下的投资组合优化，帮助在满足风险预算的同时优化收益。

title: Statistical Inference under Performativity: From Policy Feedback to Self-Evolving Systems
summary: Performativity arises when prediction-informed decisions change the data-generating process, creating feedback between deployment and learning. This phenomenon occurs in policy-making and in self-evolving AI systems that shape their own future training data. Statistical inference is challenging because estimation errors in earlier predictors affect subsequent data distributions and propagate into later updates. We develop an end-to-end framework for statistical inference under performativity. For repeated risk minimization and repeated gradient descent, we establish central limit theorems at fixed deployment rounds and derive covariance recursions that capture both current-round sampling variation and uncertainty inherited from earlier deployments. We develop consistent covariance estimators using policy perturbations and score matching. These results can yield asymptotically valid confidence regions for population iterates and the performative stable point. We further extend prediction-powered inference to this dynamic setting, combining labeled observations with predictions on additional unlabeled data to improve statistical efficiency. We evaluate our framework in synthetic, semi-synthetic educational, and self-evolving large language model routing settings. Our experiments demonstrate that ignoring propagated uncertainty can lead to substantial undercoverage even after repeated retraining. Together, these results provide statistical tools for learning systems that help determine the distributions from which they learn. Our work establish a complete statistical inference under performativity, introducing new challenges and inference settings that we believe will provide substantial value to policy-making, statistics, and machine learning.
core_methodology: The paper develops a framework for statistical inference under performativity, focusing on how prediction-informed decisions alter the data-generating process. It includes central limit theorems for repeated risk minimization and gradient descent, and introduces methods for consistent covariance estimation using policy perturbations and score matching.
data_sources: The paper evaluates its framework using synthetic data, semi-synthetic educational data, and self-evolving large language model routing settings, but does not specifically mention financial market data.
alpha_potential: The methodology could be adapted to understand and mitigate feedback effects in algorithmic trading strategies where trading decisions influence market behavior, potentially leading to more robust models in dynamic market conditions.
title_cn: 可执行性下的统计推断：从政策反馈到自演化系统
summary_cn: 本文提出了一种在可执行性（预测影响数据生成过程）下进行统计推断的框架，适用于理解交易策略对市场动态的反馈影响。通过建立中心极限定理和协方差递归，为量化交易中策略迭代和模型更新提供了统计工具，有助于开发更适应市场变化的算法交易系统。

title: TabAbax: A Tabular Foundation Model Technical Report
summary: Tabular foundation models (TFMs) enable in-context prediction on unseen tabular datasets without task-specific training. Mechanistic work has shown that increasing the depth of the ICL Transformer yields weak gains, leaving the main headroom for gains in the synthetic pretraining prior and column-row encoder upstream of the ICL backbone. We introduce TabAbax, a TFM built on TabICLv2 that focuses all modifications on these two upstream components. On the prior side, we further improve the quality and complexity of the synthetic pretraining prior. On the encoder side, a two-pass column-row stack strengthens cross-feature interactions before row compression, using learned Fourier scalar encoding from TabFM and Causilo. Evaluations on BeyondArena and TabArena show strong regression-centric gains: TabAbax reaches 1,238 Elo on the 142-dataset BeyondArena suite (10th of 41 evaluated methods), 1,676 Elo on TabArena's overall 51-dataset suite (11th of 99 methods, +115 over TabICLv2), and 2,024 Elo on TabArena's regression benchmark (7th of 99 methods, +336 over TabICLv2, +21 over TabFM). A prior-only ablation confirms the attribution: the improved prior alone yields +228 Elo for regression, demonstrating that prior quality is the dominant knob for improving regression performance.
core_methodology: Tabular foundation model (TFM) with improved synthetic pretraining prior and two-pass column-row encoder for in-context learning on tabular data without task-specific training. Focuses on regression-centric gains through enhanced prior quality and cross-feature interactions.
data_sources: Synthetic pretraining data, evaluated on BeyondArena (142 datasets) and TabArena (51 datasets) benchmark suites.
alpha_potential: Potential to identify predictive patterns in financial tabular data (e.g., fundamental data, factor exposures) for regression tasks like return prediction or risk modeling. The improved prior could learn more robust relationships from synthetic financial data.
title_cn: TabAbax: 表格基础模型技术报告
summary_cn: TabAbax是一种基于改进合成预训练先验和双通道行列编码器的表格基础模型，专注于回归任务。该模型无需特定任务训练即可在新数据集上进行预测，在金融领域可能应用于基本面分析、因子建模等表格数据预测任务，但其实际交易价值需进一步验证（当前评估均为合成数据集）。

title: World Models Need Not Be Right to Rank Policies Right: Relative Bounds and Audit Limits
summary: Selecting a reinforcement-learning (RL) policy usually requires additional environment interaction, while learned world models offer cheap but potentially biased evaluations. This raises two distinct questions: can shared model errors preserve pairwise rankings despite poor absolute values, and do they make a small number of real audits more informative? We derive an exact pairwise simulation identity and a relative bound separating common-mode Bellman residuals from policy-specific error. The analysis motivates RAVEL (Relative Auditing of Value Errors in Learned models), a selective policy tournament whose eliminations use held-out real outcomes. We test 45 SAC, TD3, and PPO policies per task in DMC cheetah-run and walker-walk. At rollout horizon 500, model rankings remain strong (Kendall tau = 0.962 and 0.800), and same-run differential-error ratios are 0.674 and 0.106. Yet mean paired audit-error correlations are only 0.007 and 0.090, and pairing changes standard deviation by -2.5 percent and +1.9 percent. Simultaneous intervals attain 99.98 percent and 99.75 percent coverage, but certify only 13.2 percent and 0 percent of decisions at eight audits. RAVEL improves low-budget walker-walk regret, whereas real-only successive halving is better at the largest budget, rejecting the precommitted twofold efficiency target. Frozen-model optimization lowers real return without increasing predicted return on average. Thus ranking fidelity, useful audit covariance, and upward model exploitation are distinct properties, separated in part by closed-loop trajectory divergence.
core_methodology: The paper introduces RAVEL (Relative Auditing of Value Errors in Learned models), a method for evaluating reinforcement-learning policies using learned world models and selective real audits. It focuses on preserving policy rankings despite model errors and uses relative bounds and audit limits to improve evaluation efficiency.
data_sources: The study uses simulated environments (DMC cheetah-run and walker-walk) to test 45 SAC, TD3, and PPO policies per task.
alpha_potential: The methodology could potentially be adapted to evaluate trading strategies in simulated market environments, but the direct application to real-world financial markets is limited due to the focus on simulated rather than financial data.

title: Do Earnings Calls Help Predict Financial Restatements? Evaluating Text Beyond Public Firm Information
summary: Financial restatements correct errors in previously published financial reports. Could managers' language in earnings calls warn of them in advance? Comparing 109 calls that precede restatements with 218 matched control calls, we find that the text predicts restatements but adds no detectable ranking gain beyond public firm information. A text classifier beats chance, largely because of restatements tied to special-purpose acquisition companies, but a model using only public information scores slightly higher. With refitting, the 95% interval for the gain from adding text (-0.05 to 0.11 AUROC) still leaves room for a meaningful benefit. A large language model scores higher, but we show that it names the exact ticker in 66% of masked transcripts, and it was released after the restatements occurred. Our results suggest that finding new warning signs in call text requires a public-information baseline and a check of what a language model already knows.
core_methodology: Text analysis of earnings calls to predict financial restatements using classifiers and large language models
data_sources: Earnings call transcripts from 109 restatement cases and 218 matched control cases
alpha_potential: Limited predictive value for restatements beyond public firm information, with slight improvement using LLMs but constrained by data leakage issues

title: Bootstrap Inference for Riemannian Optimization Problems
summary: We develop an online multiplier bootstrap for manifold-valued parameters estimated by averaging the iterates of Riemannian stochastic approximation. The method runs weighted iterations alongside the original algorithm, with each path using the same observations while updating its own state and intrinsic average. The weighted averages provide uncertainty assessments without a plug-in asymptotic covariance estimator. Under local stability and regularity conditions, we establish bootstrap consistency and show that a fixed number of paths suffices for asymptotically valid Student intervals and intrinsic confidence regions. The theory accommodates samplewise nonsmooth scores and identifies a critical oracle-bias regime in which the estimator's limiting distribution shifts, but the centered bootstrap distribution does not. Applications include spherical means, positive-definite matrix means and medians, and principal-subspace estimation. Simulations show coverage close to nominal in regular settings, and an analysis of North Atlantic storm locations illustrates descriptive online inference for a spherical center.
core_methodology: Online multiplier bootstrap for manifold-valued parameters estimated via Riemannian stochastic approximation
data_sources: Generic mathematical constructs (spherical means, positive-definite matrices, principal subspaces)
alpha_potential: Limited direct application, possibly useful for advanced statisticians working with geometric properties of financial time series

title: Solvable dynamics model of in-context learning
summary: Pretrained Transformer architectures display a surprising in-context learning ability without additional training. How the learning process guides the network to achieve this intriguing capability remains unsolved. In this study, we focus on a single-layer, single-head linear attention model, where empirical risk minimization is defined for learning. Given a finite amount of training examples, we determine the exact solution of network parameter dynamics, which is linked to the training error and generalization error, characterizing how memorization and generalization emerge from learning and how these transitions are related to curvatures of the empirical risk landscape. Furthermore, we calculate a data-dependent free energy, from which the training and generalization errors in the long-time limit of learning dynamics can be well predicted. Our work adds insights toward understanding the mechanism of in-context learning, especially from a learning dynamics perspective.
core_methodology: Analysis of learning dynamics in a simplified linear attention model for in-context learning
data_sources: Theoretical analysis with synthetic or unspecified training examples
alpha_potential: Limited direct application, but may contribute to understanding how Transformers adapt to financial data patterns

title: TreePIN$^{2}$: Tree-Prior Initialized Neural Networks
summary: Fitted decision trees provide predictive knowledge for neural network initialization. We present Tree-Prior Initialized Neural Networks (TreePIN$^{2}$), a method that translates split rules, decision paths and leaf predictions into initial network weights and biases for classification and regression. Sigmoid units encode split responses, hidden units combine them along decision paths, and leaf predictions initialize the output layer. We calibrate split softness using local training margins, sample support and impurity reduction, relating the initial responses to the data at each node. All weights and biases remain trainable, allowing gradient-based optimization to refine the transferred decisions and their combinations. Across six classification and six regression tasks with twenty paired seeds, TreePIN$^{2}$ improves mean initial and early validation performance over initialization baselines on most tasks. After fifty epochs, it achieves the best or tied-best mean validation performance among the six compared methods on ten tasks. Paired ablations show how split calibration and leaf-informed output initialization contribute to the starting predictor and its subsequent learning.
core_methodology: Initializes neural networks using decision tree structures (split rules, decision paths, leaf predictions) for improved initial and early training performance
data_sources: Generic classification and regression tasks (not finance-specific)
alpha_potential: Potential for improving model initialization in financial prediction tasks, but no demonstrated market application

title: Inference First, Training Underneath: Layer-Granular LoRA Co-Serving with LayerLoom
summary: Serving and fine-tuning a large language model on the same GPUs can turn the idle capacity between inference bursts into training progress, and low-rank adaptation (LoRA) makes this co-location cheap because both workloads read a single frozen copy of the base weights. The difficulty lies in the fine-tuning backward pass, which has no counterpart in inference. Current co-serving systems schedule backward work per serving iteration: each iteration carries a fixed backward budget, and requests that arrive in the meantime wait for it to finish, so fine-tuning dictates inference latency whenever load spikes. We observe that the backward pass of a LoRA microbatch decomposes into per-layer tasks over the same weights that the inference forward pass visits, which allows backward work to be scheduled at layer rather than iteration granularity. Building on this observation, LayerLoom attaches same-layer backward tasks to the inference forward pass and, at each layer, runs only as many of them as the latency slack of in-flight requests permits. To keep a ready task at every layer, LayerLoom maintains a wavefront of fine-tuning microbatches staggered across layers, and it bounds the wavefront's activation memory by offloading microbatch state to host memory and prefetching it ahead of the layer where the scheduler plans to use it. A fused kernel serves the paired forward and backward GEMMs from a single read of each base weight. Because all backward work of an iteration finishes within its forward pass, new requests join the next iteration as in continuous batching. On an RTX 4090 GPU running Llama-3.1-8B under a bursty production trace, LayerLoom raises joint SLO attainment by 13.5-21.8 points over prior works with fine-tuning throughput that is comparable or up to 12% higher, and it reaches the same training losses.
core_methodology: Layer-granular scheduling of backward passes for LoRA fine-tuning co-located with inference workload
data_sources: Not specified (general LLM serving context)
alpha_potential: Indirect relevance for deploying efficient adaptive models in trading environments where model updates need to coexist with low-latency inference

title: Where Causal Discovery Breaks on Real Data: Measuring the Assumptions One Property at a Time
summary: Causal discovery is usually evaluated on simulators or on systems whose ground truth follows from physics or design. When it fails on other real data, the failure is attributed to assumptions that may not hold, but which ones fail, and by how much, is rarely measured. We measure the observable properties of the data they bear on, one property at a time, on a real panel. The case study follows 2,901 US public firms over 31 quarters, with 71 types of corporate action from SEC 8-K filings, 11 financial-statement items, and an expert graph over 651 action-state pairs. The panel breaks measurable requirements of discovery: tails that survive winsorisation, balance-sheet items and revenue close to random walks, and interventions too rare to detect effects of a tenth of a standard deviation in 40 of 71 actions. Even so, a marginal test ranks expert-labelled direct above not-direct pairs within each action (AUROC 0.658) better than every null we built, so the panel does carry information about which pairs are direct. Tuned discovery methods, in configurations feasible at this panel size, recover less of it than a simple pairwise cross-correlation when pairs are ranked within each action, and no more when they are ranked within each target, which removes what the target alone predicts. Most direct pairs (132 of 222) involve actions below the support needed for 80% power against a 0.1-SD effect. For flow targets, conditioning on the target's other expert-labelled parents, often filed alongside the action, erodes the marginal discrimination, and most not-direct associations survive it: even with the graph's parent sets supplied, the expected separation does not emerge. For each property, we give a diagnostic computable before any discovery method is run.
core_methodology: Evaluation of causal discovery methods on real-world financial data by measuring observable properties and assumptions
data_sources: SEC 8-K filings and financial statements for 2,901 US public firms over 31 quarters
alpha_potential: Limited potential due to challenges in causal discovery from real financial data, including random walk behavior and rare interventions

title: Reading the Count: Prediction Markets and Brazil's 2026 Presidential Election
summary: We rebuild the public count of Brazil's 2026 presidential runoff minute by minute from the electoral court's section-level records and compare it with every trade on Kalshi and Polymarket. A projection published live on the night gave the eventual winner, Lula, a probability of 0.998 from 19:15, with 1.6% of sections counted. The markets reached 0.9 at 20:24, with 46% counted. Read as the projection's central estimate with a wider uncertainty, their prices imply a standard deviation of the final margin about four times the live projection's, and about twice that of a section-level projection calibrated on the 2018 runoff, the earlier night with the largest errors. Valued at these projections, takers' purchases of Lula after the count resumed had an expected profit of 4 to 18 cents per Kalshi contract after fees; valued at a state-level extrapolation of the count, it was zero. During a two-hour suspension of the count the markets gave Lula 0.25 to 0.44, below every reading we compute afterwards from the sections then public, none of which was available live. On the first-round night, when the headline count showed the eventual leader ahead from its first file, the same markets were faster than our projection.
core_methodology: Comparative analysis of election projection models versus prediction market prices
data_sources: Electoral court's section-level records, Kalshi and Polymarket trading data
alpha_potential: Temporal inefficiencies in prediction markets' reaction to election data

title: Quantization of Large Models with Weight Outliers and Sparsity
summary: Post-training quantization (PTQ) reduces the memory burden of large model deployment by casting the high precision trained weights to fewer bits. While this promotes memory-efficient inference, it also incurs quantization error that impairs model performance. To compensate for quantization error, the present contribution decomposes the original trained weights into a quantized matrix, a low-rank component, and a sparse matrix that accounts for outlier rows in the weights. Due to analytical intractability and the discrete structure of the decomposition, a simulated annealing search is employed to explore candidate decompositions while avoiding poor local minima. Numerical tests demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach across a broad suite of large language models, including Llama 3.2 1B, Llama 3.2 3B, Llama 3.1 8B, and Qwen2.5 7B, evaluated on natural language generation benchmarks using 4-bit NF4 and FP4 quantizers. The novel method can markedly outperform direct quantization while incurring minimal memory overhead.
core_methodology: Decomposes trained weights into quantized matrix, low-rank component, and sparse matrix for efficient quantization with simulated annealing search
data_sources: Large language models (Llama 3 series, Qwen2.5) tested on natural language generation benchmarks
alpha_potential: Potential indirect benefits for high-frequency or AI-driven strategies by enabling more efficient deployment of large LLMs

title: Efficient Conformal Calibration for Paired Recommendation Decisions
summary: Risk control can suppress useful changes to a frozen recommendation rule. We study how to recover valid activation from the same observed fractional losses. Two specified internal calibrators can lose efficiency by compressing losses into their sum or clipping auxiliary inverse counts before averaging. We propose Averaged Conformal Risk Calibration, or ACRC, which averages before clipping. A product identity proves expected-risk validity, while pointwise bounds characterize the additional activation. For fixed populations sampled without replacement, we connect activation to signed utility under heterogeneous users and switching constraints. Near the budgets, positive population mean gain and the stated nondegeneracy conditions give positive leading-order utility increments despite sampling dependence. Across six datasets, changing only calibration improves discounted net utility by $0.010226$ over raw and $0.008337$ over RB. A separately frozen Jester confirmation gives $0.011025 \pm 0.001082$ over raw with the rule and filter fixed, using a five-seed approximate 95 percent paired interval. Against information-matched SCoRE selecting risk or reward scores, the mean utility difference is $+0.015934 \pm 0.001440$. These gains use more mean realized risk within the declared budgets. Upstream failures delimit the benefit: efficient calibration releases useful modifications when the proposals themselves have value.
core_methodology: Averaged Conformal Risk Calibration (ACRC) which averages losses before clipping for efficient risk control in recommendations
data_sources: Six unspecified datasets, likely non-financial (e.g., recommendation systems)
alpha_potential: Limited direct applicability to financial markets - focuses on improving recommendation system efficiency rather than trading signals

title: Tight Stochastic Sequential Covers for General VC Classes with Unknown i.i.d. Features
summary: We study hybrid online learning with stochastic features and adversarial labels when the feature distribution is unknown. Prior work gave stochastic sequential covers of log-size $O(d\log^2 T)$ for a general VC class and logarithmic bounds only under stronger star-type structure. We show that finite VC dimension alone is enough: every binary class of VC dimension $d$ admits a distribution-blind exact cover with log-size $O(d\log T+\log(1/δ))$, matching the worst-case $Ω(d\log(T/d))$ dependence on the horizon. The key ingredient is a new local cube weight that counts Boolean subcubes incident to each realizable trace. Unlike the equal splits used in earlier constructions, we split mass unevenly according to these cube weights; a coordinate-deletion inequality shows that VC dimension controls the total cost of these splits. This yields, to our knowledge, the first tight $O((d+1)\log T)$ expected worst-case log-loss regret for general VC partitions with unknown i.i.d. features, and an exact polynomial-time implementation for planar affine halfspaces. We also show that the binary phenomenon does not extend from VC dimension to pseudo-dimension: a fixed pseudo-dimension-one sigmoid class requires $Ω(\log^2 T)$ bits for uniform sequential approximation at accuracy $1/T$.
core_methodology: Development of distribution-blind exact covers using local cube weights for VC dimension classes
data_sources: Theoretical (not specific to financial data)
alpha_potential: Limited direct application; potential theoretical framework for risk assessment in adaptive learning models

title: Regularized Wasserstein Distance for Discrete Generative Modeling and Clustering Analysis
summary: In this paper, we formulate clustering analysis as discrete generative modeling. Specifically, when the generator is restricted to a finite candidate space, the generated samples naturally emerge as the most representative prototypes of the underlying data distribution. To model such a discrete candidate space, we employ a Discrete Distribution Network (DDN). However, DDN suffers from unstable training due to its hard nearest-neighbor selection. To stabilize training and encourage geometric consistency, we replace DDN's l2 loss between images with regularized Wasserstein distance between the empirical distributions of real and generated images. The resulting framework, termed Discrete Generative Clustering (DGC), offers four notable advantages: 1) the learned cluster centers are directly interpretable, as they are realistic synthetic samples; 2) the inference cost scales logarithmically with the number of clusters, i.e., O(log K), making the method scalable to extremely large K; 3) the regularized Wasserstein distance provides a smooth and well-behaved optimization objective that facilitates stable convergence, whereas DDN's l2 loss tends to converge to poor local optima; and 4) DGC replaces DDN's nearest-neighbor selection with random-neighbor selection, which avoids the density shift problem during multi-step forward. Extensive experiments on several benchmarks demonstrate the effectiveness and desirable properties of DGC. The code is publicly available at GitHub.
core_methodology: Discrete generative modeling using regularized Wasserstein distance for clustering analysis
data_sources: Generic image benchmarks (not financial data)
alpha_potential: Potential application in clustering financial time series or asset classes, but not directly demonstrated

title: Sparse Autoencoder Attribution Graphs Are Decided at the Margin
summary: Attribution graphs over the features of sparse autoencoders (SAEs) are used to predict what an ablation does and are compared across training seeds. A TopK SAE keeps the largest preactivations at each token, and a feature's margin is its preactivation's distance to the cutoff. On five public TopK SAE pairs from three Pythia models, zeroing one feature moves a next layer feature across the cutoff in 0.74 of cases or more, and the crossings carry most of the response's energy. Over writes that scale a feature's code by three factors, the graph built on the features active beforehand has a median relative error of 0.247 or more. The margin graph adds the first order change to every preactivation and reranks, at the same cost, and errs by at most 0.033. At the median, the crossing features' decoded change is 1.24 times the model's own change in norm or more. Between seeds of one testbed, sparse maps between features explain 0.85 of a graph's energy on its active features, and 0.47 once the other seed's graph keeps only its own. The largest model studied is pythia-160m.
core_methodology: Analysis of sparse autoencoder (SAE) attribution graphs and feature margins in ablation studies
data_sources: Public TopK SAE pairs from three Pythia models (pythia-160m being the largest)
alpha_potential: Limited to theoretical insights on feature attribution in neural networks rather than financial market applications

title: Guarded Compression of Adam Optimizer State with Shared-Gradient Bounds
summary: Adam keeps two FP32 moments per parameter, twice the bytes of the FP32 weights, yet compressing them is risky: the update divides by the square root of the second moment, so small reconstruction errors can change the restored computation substantially. We study guarded moment compression, in which a coordinate's decoded moments are accepted only if they reproduce the native FP32 Adam update to within a tolerance $τ$, in units of the learning rate, for every gradient in a clipped domain; all other coordinates are stored exactly. The natural certificate, which ranges each update separately over gradient intervals, fails: on one million trained OPT-125M coordinates it escapes 98.9% of coordinates and the payload grows to 126.6% of raw FP32. Our key observation is that both updates consume the same gradient and parameter. Bounding their difference directly, with FP32 rounding-error allowances and a fixed mixed linear-logarithmic gradient partition, cuts escapes to 0.53% and the payload to 28.3% at $τ=0.01$. Across 120 complete-checkpoint restores of OPT-125M and ResNet-18, with four trained seeds and three training fractions per model, guarded 8-bit log codes shrink moment payloads by 69.5% and 71.9% relative to FP32, 40.8% and 45.4% relative to equally guarded BF16, and 29.3% and 37.6% relative to equally guarded blockwise 8-bit, and every restored first update stays within tolerance. Encoding and restoration together take 2.3-2.6$\times$ as long as guarded BF16 but less time than guarded blockwise 8-bit. Searching both moment codes jointly saves under 0.001% more bytes at 6% more codec time, so per-moment rounding suffices. The guarantee covers the first restored update under a pinned Torch operation model; we measure subsequent training empirically.
core_methodology: Guarded moment compression for Adam optimizer state to reduce memory usage while maintaining update accuracy within a specified tolerance
data_sources: Not applicable (focused on optimization technique rather than financial data)
alpha_potential: Potential to improve efficiency of training AI models used in trading strategies, but no direct trading application
